set_aside.subject: operation_element_conclusion
set_aside.text: operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] MUST decide in these five steps, the first that holds concluding, and MUST NOT conclude anything merely because the element has no NodeExecution. Step 1, only when the element has at least one NodeExecution: its latest one, the one with the highest attempt_number, concludes succeeded with that record's outputs when it succeeded; when it is outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied, succeeded with no outputs if the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; when its status is any other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown, failed with that status and detail_code. Step 2, whether or not the element has any NodeExecution: an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id, since the first approval of an element is requested before it has any NodeExecution; after an attempt resolved not_applied only an approval whose attempt_number is greater than that of the element's latest attempt so resolved counts, the same attempt rule find_send_authority applies to approvals. Step 3: a latest outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown. Step 4: a latest service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable. Step 5, only when steps 2 to 4 found nothing: the element is not reached, which covers an element with no NodeExecution and no such approval and a latest outcome_unknown whose attempt the owner resolved not_applied; it is reached again when its node is next taken, and after not_applied its send needs a fresh approval (find_send_authority), which reach_operation_element requests (decision 32).

When the SendResult outcome is succeeded MUST store the outputs before writing: each JSON output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant turns the outcome into contract_violation with detail value_too_large and no outputs; otherwise each JSON output is published with put_value_bytes — its value_digest is content_identity of a BytesContent holding the bytes, the digest put_value_bytes returns; its value_id is content_identity of the StoredValueContent, computed here and never compared with what put_value_bytes returns — and becomes a StoredValue of value carriage with the output port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items), its size and the class the binding declares for that port, and a file output is published with spool_file under SpooledFileKey of the run, node, map_index, this attempt_number, the port and no list_index, becoming a SpooledFile of the port's declared class, which every port of a binding has, since a proposal leaving out a port's class is refused (A08 rule 5, M01), so that class is always a DisclosureClass member; a RefusedError from spool_file turns the outcome into contract_violation with no outputs, a non-read binding's attempt still applied (a read binding has no attempt).

set_aside.subject: operation_element_conclusion
set_aside.text: operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] MUST decide in these five steps, the first that holds concluding, and MUST NOT conclude anything merely because the element has no NodeExecution. Step 1, only when the element has at least one NodeExecution: its latest one, the one with the highest attempt_number, concludes succeeded with that record's outputs when it succeeded; when it is outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied, succeeded with no outputs if the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; when its status is any other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown, failed with that status and detail_code. Step 2, whether or not the element has any NodeExecution: an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id, since the first approval of an element is requested before it has any NodeExecution; after an attempt resolved not_applied only an approval whose attempt_number is greater than that of the element's latest attempt so resolved counts, the same attempt rule find_send_authority applies to approvals. Step 3: a latest outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown. Step 4: a latest service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable. Step 5, only when steps 2 to 4 found nothing: the element is not reached, which covers an element with no NodeExecution and no such approval and a latest outcome_unknown whose attempt the owner resolved not_applied; it is reached again when its node is next taken, and after not_applied its send needs a fresh approval (find_send_authority), which reach_operation_element requests (decision 32).

set_aside.subject: reach_operation_element
set_aside.text: reach_operation_element: [BEHAVIOR] When find_send_authority returns None MUST, unless an approval of the element with status requested already exists — for a resend after not_applied only one whose attempt_number is greater than that of the element's latest attempt resolved not_applied, the same attempt rule find_send_authority applies to approvals, so an approval requested before that resolution never counts —, write one RequestApprovalChange for the element with the binding_id, input_digests, the prepared request_digest and an ApprovalPreview of the operation's service_id, operation_name and effect_class, the prepared request description and the element's input PortRefs; input_digests are the digests of every input value and file in input port name order, list elements in list order. Nothing is sent and the element waits with reason owner_approval for that approval, the existing requested one when there was one, even if its request_digest differs. Since nothing was sent, no NodeExecution is written: an element waiting for its first approval has none, and operation_element_conclusion concludes ElementWaiting from the requested approval, so the run takes the element again only after the owner decides.

set_aside.subject: recover_in_flight_attempts
set_aside.text: recover_in_flight_attempts: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read every EffectAttempt with status in_flight through read_records with AttemptsByStatus and handle them oldest first in store order, one RecoverInFlightChange per attempt written with an Actor of kind kernel; the change turns the attempt unknown with concluded_at the recovery time, carries used_approval_id only when the attempt's authority is an ApprovalAuthority, and carries an execution only when RecordsByAttempt with when_missing omit finds no NodeExecution for that attempt key. No service is contacted, nothing is sent again and no outcome is inferred; a grant or flow activation authority changes no record but the attempt and its NodeExecution.
